rows.title: CPU metrics
Kernel: CPU time by mode, grouped by $pmu_by (cpuN when grouped by shard)

panels.spec/description: rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="system"}), averaged over CPUs. Kernel time outside interrupts. This kernel samples the user/system split at each 1 ms tick (no nohz_full), so a shift between them need not mean extra kernel work: check user + system per task.
rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="softirq"}), averaged over CPUs. Time in softirqs, mostly network receive (including packets RPS steers from CPU 0).
rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="user"}), averaged over CPUs. User-mode time. Includes the reactor's idle polling, so it stays high on a lightly loaded node; use Reactor busy for load.
rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}), averaged over CPUs. Time the CPU slept: the reactor's idle sleep. Zero means the shard never ran out of work.
rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="iowait"}), averaged over CPUs. Idle time with I/O outstanding. Seastar uses AIO, so this stays near zero.
rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="steal"}), averaged over CPUs. Time the hypervisor reports it ran something else on this vCPU. Graviton guests report 0 even when the host slows them down.

rows.title: PMU: core efficiency (nodes running pmu-textfile), grouped by $pmu_by

panels.spec/description: inst_retired / cpu_cycles (perf group i). Exact: a ratio of counters from the same perf group, counted over the same time slices. Drops when each instruction gets slower; read it with the memory-stall panel.

panels.spec/title: Memory-stall share of cycles: stall_backend_mem / cpu_cycles [exact]
panels.spec/description: stall_backend_mem / cpu_cycles (perf group m). Exact: a ratio of counters from the same perf group, counted over the same time slices. stall_backend_mem / cpu_cycles: cycles the backend waited on memory.

panels.spec/title: Kernel share of busy cycles, shard CPUs: cpu_cycles:k / (cpu_cycles:u + cpu_cycles:k) [exact]
panels.spec/description: cpu_cycles:k / (cpu_cycles:u + cpu_cycles:k) (perf group i). Exact: a ratio of counters from the same perf group, counted over the same time slices. cpu_cycles:k / (cpu_cycles:u + cpu_cycles:k) on CPUs running a shard, both in group i, so exact. The hardware filters by privilege level, so tick sampling cannot bias it; compare with system time in the Kernel row. Excludes idle (cycles stop in WFI) and hypervisor time. Empty before the user-only feeder was deployed.

panels.spec/title: Kernel share of busy cycles, CPUs without a shard: cpu_cycles:k / (cpu_cycles:u + cpu_cycles:k) [exact]
panels.spec/description: cpu_cycles:k / (cpu_cycles:u + cpu_cycles:k) (perf group i). Exact: a ratio of counters from the same perf group, counted over the same time slices. The same ratio on CPUs that run no shard (shard="none"): the interrupt CPU, mostly kernel. Kept apart so it does not dominate the shard panel when grouped by instance.

panels.spec/title: L2 misses per 1000 instructions: 1000 × l2d_cache_lmiss_rd / inst_retired [approx]
panels.spec/description: 1000 × l2d_cache_lmiss_rd / inst_retired (perf groups m+i). Approximate: a ratio across perf groups, which are counted in alternating time slices. Flat while IPC drops means the workload misses as often but each miss takes longer: contention outside the guest. Rising means our working set changed, or (above ~85% reactor busy) that idle-polling instructions vanished; prefer the per-read panels then.
panels.spec/data/spec/queries/0/spec/query/spec: 1000 * (sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="l2d_cache_lmiss_rd",mode=~"$pmumode|",group="m"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="cpu_cycles",mode=~"$pmumode|",group="m"}[$__rate_interval]))) / (sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="inst_retired",mode=~"$pmumode|",group="i"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="cpu_cycles",mode=~"$pmumode|",group="i"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.spec/title: Memory-stall cycles per replica read: stall_backend_mem / replica reads
panels.spec/description: stall_backend_mem / replica reads (perf group m). Scaled count: perf scales it up for the time its group was off the counters; accurate for steady load. Polling adds almost no memory stalls, so unlike IPC this compares nodes fairly. Same work, more cycles per read: slower memory.

panels.spec/title: L2 misses per replica read: l2d_cache_lmiss_rd / replica reads
panels.spec/description: l2d_cache_lmiss_rd / replica reads (perf group m). Scaled count: perf scales it up for the time its group was off the counters; accurate for steady load. Polling-independent miss rate. Flat while memory-stall cycles per read rise: each miss got more expensive (neighbour or placement).

panels.spec/title: Share of L1 data refills from main memory (uncalibrated): l1d_cache_refill_outer / (l1d_cache_refill_inner + l1d_cache_refill_outer) [exact]
panels.spec/description: l1d_cache_refill_outer / (l1d_cache_refill_inner + l1d_cache_refill_outer) (perf group o). Exact: a ratio of counters from the same perf group, counted over the same time slices. L1D_CACHE_REFILL_OUTER / (INNER + OUTER), both in group o. The Neoverse V2 manual counts a refill as inner when the data comes from this core's L2, the chip's shared cache (SLC) or another core's cache, so outer should mean main memory (DRAM). Not yet confirmed by a calibration test. A rise at flat load suggests the shared cache holds less of our data. Misleading above ~85% reactor busy: idle polling makes most L2-sourced refills, so when it stops the share jumps with no change in DRAM traffic; check the per-read panel.

panels.spec/title: L1 data refills from main memory per replica read (uncalibrated): l1d_cache_refill_outer / replica reads
panels.spec/description: l1d_cache_refill_outer / replica reads (perf group o). Scaled count: perf scales it up for the time its group was off the counters; accurate for steady load. Main-memory refills per unit of work. Unlike the share panel, idle polling does not distort it: a rise means each read pulls more data from DRAM (e.g. the shared cache holding less of it).

panels.spec/title: Share of L2 write-backs that are snoop responses: l2d_cache_wb_clean / (l2d_cache_wb_victim + l2d_cache_wb_clean) [exact]
panels.spec/description: l2d_cache_wb_clean / (l2d_cache_wb_victim + l2d_cache_wb_clean) (perf group w). Exact: a ratio of counters from the same perf group, counted over the same time slices. l2d_cache_wb_clean / (wb_victim + wb_clean): write-backs that are snoop responses (another core reading this core's data, or the interconnect reclaiming lines) rather than evictions.

rows.title: PMU: memory bandwidth, grouped by $pmu_by

panels.spec/title: Traffic between L2 and memory: 64 B × (l2d_cache_lmiss_rd + l2d_cache_wb_victim)
panels.spec/description: 64 B × (l2d_cache_lmiss_rd + l2d_cache_wb_victim) (perf groups m+w). Scaled count: perf scales it up for the time its group was off the counters; accurate for steady load. (l2d_cache_lmiss_rd + l2d_cache_wb_victim) x 64 B: lines fetched into L2 (loads and store misses) plus dirty lines evicted. Upper bound on DRAM traffic (SLC hits included); misses prefetch fills and full-line streaming writes. Estimates the instance's own load on the shared L3 and memory; a 4-core i8g share of socket DRAM bandwidth is about 22 GB/s.

panels.spec/title: L2 incoming bandwidth from misses: 64 B × l2d_cache_lmiss_rd
panels.spec/description: 64 B × l2d_cache_lmiss_rd (perf group m). Scaled count: perf scales it up for the time its group was off the counters; accurate for steady load. l2d_cache_lmiss_rd x 64 B: lines filled into L2 from outside the core (SLC, another core's L2 or DRAM). Includes store misses, which fetch the line as a read (ReadUnique). Excludes hardware-prefetch fills and, possibly, instruction fetches. A 4-core i8g share of socket DRAM bandwidth is about 22 GB/s; one core can pull about 30 GB/s from the SLC.

panels.spec/title: Dirty evictions to memory: 64 B × l2d_cache_wb_victim
panels.spec/description: 64 B × l2d_cache_wb_victim (perf group w). Scaled count: perf scales it up for the time its group was off the counters; accurate for steady load. l2d_cache_wb_victim (r56) x 64 B: dirty lines evicted from L2 to make room, headed for the SLC or DRAM.

64 B × l2d_cache_wb_clean (perf group w). Scaled count: perf scales it up for the time its group was off the counters; accurate for steady load. l2d_cache_wb_clean (r57) x 64 B: lines this L2 supplies on a snoop, clean or dirty: another core reading a line held here, a direct transfer the interconnect forwards here, or a cache maintenance operation.

panels.spec/title: L1 data refill bandwidth from main memory (uncalibrated): 64 B × l1d_cache_refill_outer
panels.spec/description: 64 B × l1d_cache_refill_outer (perf group o). Scaled count: perf scales it up for the time its group was off the counters; accurate for steady load. L1D_CACHE_REFILL_OUTER x 64 B: data lines brought into the L1 data cache from main memory, if the manual's reading holds.

rows.title: PMU: per L2 read miss, grouped by $pmu_by

panels.spec/title: Stall cycles per L2 miss: stall_backend_mem / l2d_cache_lmiss_rd [exact]
panels.spec/description: stall_backend_mem / l2d_cache_lmiss_rd (perf group m). Exact: a ratio of counters from the same perf group, counted over the same time slices. stall_backend_mem / l2d_cache_lmiss_rd, both in group m, so exact. Rises when the shared L3 hit rate falls or DRAM gets slower.

panels.spec/title: Snoop write-backs per L2 read miss: l2d_cache_wb_clean / l2d_cache_lmiss_rd [approx]
panels.spec/description: l2d_cache_wb_clean / l2d_cache_lmiss_rd (perf groups w+m). Approximate: a ratio across perf groups, which are counted in alternating time slices. Normalised by work: cross-shard sharing scales with load, so a rise at flat misses per read points outside our own sharing, e.g. shared lines no longer in the SLC being served from a core's L2.

panels.spec/title: L1 data refills from main memory per L2 read miss (uncalibrated): l1d_cache_refill_outer / l2d_cache_lmiss_rd [approx]
panels.spec/description: l1d_cache_refill_outer / l2d_cache_lmiss_rd (perf groups o+m). Approximate: a ratio across perf groups, which are counted in alternating time slices. L1D_CACHE_REFILL_OUTER over L2D_CACHE_LMISS_RD: roughly, the fraction of L2 misses that go all the way to main memory. The two counters count different traffic (L2 misses also include L2 prefetches, instruction fetches and page-table walks), so prefetchers backing off can raise this with no change in where data comes from. Read it next to the share panel.
panels.spec/data/spec/queries/0/spec/query/spec: (sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="l1d_cache_refill_outer",mode=~"$pmumode|",group="o"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="cpu_cycles",mode=~"$pmumode|",group="o"}[$__rate_interval]))) / (sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="l2d_cache_lmiss_rd",mode=~"$pmumode|",group="m"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="cpu_cycles",mode=~"$pmumode|",group="m"}[$__rate_interval])))

rows.title: PMU: bus traffic, user and kernel together, grouped by $pmu_by

panels.spec/title: Bus read beats per second: bus_access_rd
panels.spec/description: bus_access_rd (perf group b). Scaled count: perf scales it up for the time its group was off the counters; accurate for steady load. BUS_ACCESS_RD: data beats on the read channel between the core and the interconnect, user and kernel together. Reads from the SLC, DRAM or another core all cross it. Arm does not state the beat width; on Neoverse V2 it is most likely 32 B, i.e. two beats per 64 B line (unverified).

panels.spec/title: Bus write beats per second: bus_access_wr
panels.spec/description: bus_access_wr (perf group b). Scaled count: perf scales it up for the time its group was off the counters; accurate for steady load. BUS_ACCESS_WR: data beats on the write channel: write-backs of dirty lines and other data the core sends out, user and kernel together.

panels.spec/title: Snoop data-response beats per second: bus_access - bus_access_rd - bus_access_wr
panels.spec/description: bus_access - bus_access_rd - bus_access_wr (perf group b). Scaled count: perf scales it up for the time its group was off the counters; accurate for steady load. BUS_ACCESS - BUS_ACCESS_RD - BUS_ACCESS_WR. Arm defines BUS_ACCESS as the sum of read beats, write beats and snoop data responses, so the difference is the data this core sends in answer to snoops: the byte-level counterpart of L2D_CACHE_WB_CLEAN, in all modes.
panels.spec/data/spec/queries/0/spec/query/spec: sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="bus_access",mode="",group="b"}[$__rate_interval])) - sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="bus_access_rd",mode="",group="b"}[$__rate_interval])) - sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="bus_access_wr",mode="",group="b"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.spec/title: Share of bus beats that are snoop data responses: (bus_access - bus_access_rd - bus_access_wr) / bus_access [exact]
panels.spec/description: (bus_access - bus_access_rd - bus_access_wr) / bus_access (perf group b). Exact: a ratio of counters from the same perf group, counted over the same time slices. Snoop data-response beats over all bus beats, all three counters in group b. Rises when other agents read lines this core holds, independently of how busy the core is.
panels.spec/data/spec/queries/0/spec/query/spec: (sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="bus_access",mode="",group="b"}[$__rate_interval])) - sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="bus_access_rd",mode="",group="b"}[$__rate_interval])) - sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="bus_access_wr",mode="",group="b"}[$__rate_interval]))) / sum by ($pmu_by) (rate(node_pmu_events_total{cluster="$cluster",instance=~"[[node]]",dc=~"$dc",rack=~"$rack",event="bus_access",mode="",group="b"}[$__rate_interval]))

rows.title: ethtool limitations - only applicable if ethtool is enabled on nodetool_exporter

panels.spec/description: Outbound bandwidth allowance exceed events per second — the rate at which the NIC attempts to transmit above its allowed egress bandwidth limit (often indicating throttling/shaping).
Inbound bandwidth allowance exceed events per second — the rate at which the NIC receives above its allowed ingress bandwidth limit (often indicating ingress shaping/throttling).

Conntrack allowance exceed events per second — the rate at which the system/NIC exceeds its allowed connection-tracking (conntrack) limit, often indicating connection pressure and potential drops or throttling.

Link-local allowance exceed events per second — the rate at which the NIC exceeds its allowed link-local traffic limit (e.g., ARP/ND or other local control traffic), often indicating local-network chatter and possible throttling
